topic: Eligible Canadian dividends: 38% gross-up and 15.0198% federal dividend tax credit; with no other income, about $80,000 of eligible dividends pays $0 federal tax in 2026 (example)

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): single person, 2026, no other income, eligible dividends from taxable Canadian corporations; federal brackets 14% to $58,523, 20.5% to $117,045; BPA $16,452 x 14% = $2,303; tax on $110,400 = $18,828; DTC 15.0198% x $110,400 = $16,582 >= $16,525 -> $0 federal tax (credit is non-refundable). Salary comparison: $80,000 employment income, federal tax after BPA, CPP/EI and Canada employment credits = $9,243 (longform th() model). Provincial tax, Ontario health premium and other income not included; break-even ≈ $80,755 of eligible dividends. VO rounds $9,243 to 'about nine thousand, two hundred' (salary_fed_r).

spoken.taxable: a hundred and ten thousand, four hundred

sources.dtc: canada.ca CRA line 40425 Federal dividend tax credit: eligible dividends grossed up by 38%; credit = 15.0198% of the taxable amount on line 12000 (via search 2026-11-01)
